why: The trie itself: one node per prefix, children keyed by the next character, and an end-of-word flag. search and startsWith walk the same path and differ only in whether they require that flag at the end.
hints: Many words share prefixes. How could you store them so a shared prefix is stored once?
Each node is a map from character to child plus an end flag. insert walks and creates nodes; search walks and checks the flag; startsWith walks and only checks that the path exists.
Nested dicts or a small Node class. Every operation costs O(length of the word), independent of how many words are stored.
pitfalls: search("do") is false after inserting only "dog": a prefix path is not a word without the end flag.
Inserting the same word twice changes nothing.
